finding.claim: The authenticated identity is taken directly from a client-supplied HTTP header with no verification, so any caller can impersonate any user and pass the ACL checks. The header name suggests an upstream proxy sets it, but nothing in this code strips, signs, or validates it. It is exploitable if the app is reachable without a proxy that overwrites the header.
finding.sink: ensure_allowed/is_allowed grant lookup guarding file deletion (views.py:17-18) and rename (views.py:25-27)

trace.note: g.user = request.headers.get('X-Session-User-Verified') with no signature, session or secret check
delete_file loads the file by fid
ensure_allowed(g.user, f, 'delete') trusts the spoofed identity
is_allowed returns True if action is in resource['grants'][user]; the user key is the attacker-chosen string
del STORE[fid] runs, so the file is deleted as the impersonated owner
rename_file likewise lets the attacker overwrite f['name'] after is_allowed passes

finding.guards_checked: Checked acl.py and views.py. The only guard is the per-resource grants lookup, which is sound but keyed on the spoofable identity. There is no authentication decorator, no signature or HMAC check, no proxy-trust check such as a shared secret or mTLS, and no stripping of the header. No other files exist in the directory. A None user does not match any grants key, so omitting the header is denied; the bypass requires guessing or knowing a granted username.

verdict.guard_found: Only the per-resource grants check (acl.py:5, ensure_allowed aborts 403 at acl.py:9-10, is_allowed tested at views.py:25). It works correctly but is keyed on the spoofable identity. There is no authentication, signature, or header stripping.
verdict.reason: views.py:11 sets g.user straight from a client-supplied header, and acl.py:5 only looks that string up in resource grants, so an anonymous caller who knows a granted username can pass views.py:17 and views.py:25 and delete or rename files. This holds only if no upstream proxy overwrites the header, and nothing in the code shows one.
